subject: PrivNet: observed control-plane state divergence during 2/15 upgrade — actions & evidence
messages:
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: alex.silver@novamed.health, ops@novamed.health
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-02-15T21:03:00Z
Subject: PrivNet: observed control-plane state divergence during 2/15 upgrade — initial note

Hi Alex / NovaMed ops team,

Quick update from our side — during the 02/15 midnight PrivNet upgrade we observed a small cohort of control-plane nodes reporting divergent state for agent handshake metadata (operator table mismatches). This led to transient reconnect attempts and elevated latency for a subset of inference requests routed through your private VPC region.

Immediate actions taken (completed):
- Rolled back the upgrade on the control-plane side for the B pool by 21:00 UTC.
- Forced A/B routing to stable model proxies to avoid further reconnections.
- Collected full control-plane state dumps and agent handshake logs (attached).

Why this happened (prelim): a sequencing edge-case in the orchestration commit that allowed two concurrent leader-ack windows to apply conflicting entries during the upgrade window. We are treating this as an integrity divergence and prioritizing evidence collection.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Run binary-free verification on node state and reconcile to authoritative snapshot.
2) Provide you with a short P1 evidence packet and a bridge-call this afternoon to walk through logs and mitigations.
3) Follow up with a postmortem and permanent guardrail.

I have attached the handshake log excerpt and a control-plane state dump for your ops team to review. Would 14:00 PT tomorrow for a 30-min bridge work for you for a first-pass review?

Apologies for the interruption — we know predictability is critical. We're treating this as high priority.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: privnet-handshake-log-0215.txt, controlplane-state-dump-0215.tar.gz
From: alex.silver@novamed.health
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@novamed.health
Date: 2028-02-15T21:28:00Z
Subject: Re: PrivNet: observed control-plane state divergence during 2/15 upgrade — initial note

Thanks Sofia — appreciate the quick flag.

Confirmed we saw elevated retries on our end between 20:45–21:05 UTC; no user-facing failures reported but internal queue backlog increased. We can take the artifacts and have our infra team look concurrently. 14:00 PT tomorrow works for us.

Two asks for the call:
- Please bring the authority that can walk through the leader-election timeline (SRE or runtime lead).
- Clarify whether any customer data was at risk; specifically, were any request payloads retried to a different tenant endpoint during the period?

Alex Silver
Director of Platform Engineering
NovaMed Health
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.silver@novamed.health, ops@novamed.health
Date: 2028-02-16T02:11:00Z
Subject: Re: PrivNet: observed control-plane state divergence during 2/15 upgrade — initial note

(Internal note, looping SRE and CS)

Hey team — I pulled the artifacts. Initial triage: 1) logs show leader-ack collision windows at ~20:47–20:52 UTC on 3 control-plane replicas; 2) agent handshakes retried but include tenant id binding — I don’t see evidence that any tenant traffic was accepted by the wrong tenant proxy. Jordan, can you confirm the reconciliation plan?

I'll prep a short customer-facing evidence packet containing: problem statement, timeline, affected node IDs, list of artifacts and a scrubbed log excerpt for NovaMed. Will keep language concise and non-technical for exec readership.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.silver@novamed.health, ops@novamed.health, support@infra-partner.com
Date: 2028-02-16T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: PrivNet: observed control-plane state divergence during 2/15 upgrade — initial note

On Thu, Feb 16, 2028 at 02:11, marissa_cole@redwood.ai wrote:
> (Internal note, looping SRE and CS)
>
> Hey team — I pulled the artifacts. Initial triage: 1) logs show leader-ack collision windows at ~20:47–20:52 UTC on 3 control-plane replicas; 2) agent handshakes retried but include tenant id binding — I don’t see evidence that any tenant traffic was accepted by the wrong tenant proxy. Jordan, can you confirm the reconciliation plan?

Hi all — here's the technical reconciliation plan we executed and items outstanding:

Executed (night window):
- Snapshot-and-verify: took authoritative snapshot from control-plane leader at 21:10 UTC and ran a binary verification across B pool nodes.
- Forced reconverge: applied canonical snapshot to two divergent replicas; confirmed successful compare checksums.
- routed traffic away from nodes with non-matching KV checksums until verification completed.

Outstanding actions (today):
- Deep scrub of KV diffs to determine root commit sequence. Estimated completion: EOD 02/16.
- Hotfix proposal to prevent concurrent ack windows is with runtime team; expected PR by end of week.
- Produce a concise evidence packet for NovaMed (Marissa to coordinate wording).

On the data exposure question: we do not see any evidence of cross-tenant traffic acceptance. Handshakes that retried kept tenant binding intact; there were retries but no proxy reassignment to a different tenant. We will include verification artifacts in the packet.

I’ll be on the 14:00 PT bridge as the SRE lead to walk through sequence diagrams and checksums. Jordan Blake
SRE Lead — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: alex.silver@novamed.health, ops@novamed.health
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, support@infra-partner.com
Date: 2028-02-16T14:22:00Z
Subject: PrivNet follow-up: evidence packet and next steps (post-bridge)

Alex / NovaMed ops — thanks again for the bridge earlier. Summarizing what we covered and the immediate customer-facing artifacts attached.

Summary / what we confirmed:
- Incident window: 2028-02-15 20:45–21:05 UTC.
- Root cause (prelim): sequencing edge-case in the orchestration commit that allowed concurrent leader-ack windows to create transient KV divergence on a small set of control-plane replicas.
- Impact: elevated retries and latency for a fraction (~0.7%) of private VPC requests routed through affected replicas; no evidence of cross-tenant request acceptance.

Artifacts attached (zipped):
- controlplane-state-dump-0215.tar.gz (authoritative snapshots and per-node checksums)
- privnet-handshake-log-0215.txt (filtered, scrubbed for PII)
- bridgecall-recording-20280216.mp3 (recording of 14:00 PT session)

Remediation & timeline:
- Completed: rollback of B-pool upgrade; forced reconverge to authoritative snapshot; traffic routing changes applied.
- Short-term (this week): runtime team to land a guardrail preventing overlapping ack windows and add a health-check to detect checksum divergence earlier. Target: PR by 2028-02-19, test pass by 02-22.
- Long-term: planned orchestration change to make leader-ack an atomic step (design in Q2).

We’ll open a formal postmortem once the hotfix is validated; Marissa will send a customer-ready executive one pager and I’ll include the technical appendix with checksums. If you want our security team to do a second independent verification, we can schedule that as well.

Next actions for NovaMed: please confirm you received the attached zip and whether you'd like security verification.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments included: controlplane-state-dump-0215.tar.gz, privnet-handshake-log-0215.txt, bridgecall-recording-20280216.mp3
